strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds a runtime-owned aggregate task-set progress graph on the existing task.list response.
Lets headless callers choose runnable, blocked, terminal, and parent-join-ready next actions without reconstructing task graph policy outside the runtime.
Surfaces parent/child task graph edges and parent-join-ready task IDs from controlled child provenance.
Keeps task graph classification and next-action policy in Rust while the VSIX only validates the bounded protocol shape.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances progress_visualization directly, with support for headless_autonomous_development, subtask_orchestration, and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: Existing task.list now returns progress_overview with runtime-owned parent/child graph nodes and edges, runnable task IDs, blocked task IDs, terminal task IDs, parent-join-ready task IDs, bounded next-action sets, status/stage counts, and a replay-safe aggregate source_fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before M10.2 a caller could inspect one run, but could not ask the runtime for a bounded view of a task set. Repeating run.inspect across every task would duplicate policy outside the runtime and encourage full-ledger-per-task wrappers.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless controllers and future VSIX progress UI would still need to infer parent-child graph state, runnable work, blocked work, and join-ready parents from fragmented task records or per-run inspection.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M9.6 materialized selected index context, M10.1 classified one inspected run/task, and PR #154 finished the single-run progress snapshot. M10.2 aggregates a multi-task graph and action set on task.list without adding live observation.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase reuses task.list and adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: No. A single progress_overview is necessary because callers need one runtime-owned aggregate contract for the listed task set; it is not a report, digest, readiness wrapper, history, or verdict.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime now classifies the listed task records into graph nodes, parent/child edges, bounded lifecycle/stage/action groups, parent-join consumption-aware ready IDs, and aggregate fingerprints instead of returning only raw TaskRecord rows.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled or headless controller can read task.list once, find explicit runnable/blocked/terminal/join-ready task IDs, and decide the next bounded action without scanning every ledger or reimplementing runtime policy.
answers.milestone_progress: Moves M10 from single-run progress snapshots toward a usable runtime-owned progress visualization substrate for multi-task autonomous development.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M10.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm runtime-owned aggregate task-set progress on task.list, not a per-task run.inspect wrapper or VSIX-owned graph policy.

exit_criteria: Existing task.list returns tasks plus progress_overview
progress_overview includes runtime-owned graph nodes and parent/child edges from controlled child provenance
progress_overview includes runnable_task_ids, blocked_task_ids, terminal_task_ids, and parent_join_ready_task_ids
progress_overview includes bounded next_action_sets and blocked_sets using existing progress enums
progress_overview includes status and stage counts but no arbitrary percentage
progress_overview includes a SHA-256 source_fingerprint over bounded derived task-set state
Completed parents with terminal controlled children report parent_join_ready and run_parent_task_explicitly
Completed parents with terminal controlled children and consumed parent-join continuation evidence do not report parent_join_ready and fall back to explicit parent inspection
Completed parents with runnable pending children report completed_with_pending_children and run_remaining_child_tasks_explicitly
Completed parents with non-runnable children report inspect_non_runnable_child_tasks
task.list remains read-only and appends no ledger event
task.list does not execute tasks, consume parent-join state, call providers, read workspace files, apply patches, run verifiers, or start an async executor
The aggregate is not produced by calling run.inspect for every task or by scanning every task ledger
VSIX protocol validators accept valid task.list progress_overview values and reject missing overview, invalid enums, raw fields, and arbitrary percentage fields

No new JSON-RPC method, diagnostics wrapper, report, digest, history, readiness, preview, live progress observer, asynchronous executor, mutation, shell/git/network/service action, or VSIX policy inference is added

test_tokens: rejects task.list results without progress overview

next_phase_candidate_notes: M10.3 may add live concurrent progress observation only after a separate safety design. M10.2 intentionally stops at aggregate persisted task-set progress and keeps async execution, automatic task execution, and live observation out of scope.
